_about: Lamp upload rules (render/lamp_flicker.rs, read by world_mesh::lamps()). prop_budget: how many lit props one floor's lamp list keeps; `default` is the baseline (the original's 10) and `level.<n>` raises it on a storey whose window holds many lamps (the sewers). The shader still lights each frame with the 16 nearest (shader::MAX_LAMPS). room_flicker: region id -> { hz, depth } for the switchable room lights of rooms in that region (hz: cycles a second, depth: 0..1 swing of the energy either way; a missing region is steady). A prop's own light takes flicker_hz and flicker_depth in data/props/*.json. Each lamp's start phase is drawn from its place in the world, so neighbours do not pulse together. Nothing flickers while the reduced motion setting is on. room_tint: `region.<id>` or `type.<room type>` -> { color "#rrggbb" (multiplies the lamp's colour: near white keeps it, so this is a temperature shift), energy (multiplies its energy, default 1) } for every lamp in a room of that region or type; a type row wins over its region's. dark_rooms.fraction: the share of level 0 rooms (Infinite route) that start with their lamps off, chosen by room id (Godot's default_room_light, about 1 in 4); 0 turns it off. It ships at 0: streamed windows have no light switch, so a dark room would stay dim for the whole run. lamp_cap: the most lamps the shader lights with, by graphics quality (`default`, or LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / AUTO), at most 16.
_prop_glow: prop_glow_budget: how many of a floor's lit props may be screen glows (a prop light with `glow: true` in data/props/*.json: arcade cabinets, vending machines, TVs, consoles); they come out of prop_budget, never on top of it, and the real lamps keep the rest. Both groups are chosen nearest the runner (nearest the window's centre when a list is built without one), and chosen again once the runner has walked prop_reselect_distance metres.
